title: Agricultural curve premia on free data
ask: Do agricultural curve premia work on free data?
reason: No contract data; the proxy only matched plain momentum.
hypothesis: The change in an agricultural futures curve's slope predicts returns beyond plain momentum.
question: Basis-momentum, the change in the gap between the first and second futures contracts, is reported to predict commodity returns. Can we test it on free data for grains and softs?
prior: The published Sharpe is 0.8 or more, but a clean test needs daily prices for every expired contract, which free sources may not have.
citations: Boons, M. & Prado, M. P. (2019). Basis-Momentum. Journal of Finance 74(1).
method: Data gate first: could free sources rebuild front and second-month prices from 2007?

When the gate failed, a pre-registered proxy: the change in a commodity fund's curve-blended price against its front future, two trials (the proxy and plain 12-month momentum), 2011 to 2026, net of one tick a side and two ticks a roll, at 8% volatility.
Bar fixed in advance: net Sharpe at least 0.30, bootstrap 5th percentile above −0.20, at least 0.10 above plain momentum, positive in both halves.
verdict_reason: The data gate failed: no free source gives prices for expired contracts, so true coverage since 2007 is under 1%. The proxy then earned net Sharpe 0.21, the same as plain 12-month momentum, with a bootstrap 5th percentile of −0.23. Its profit came from sugar and soybeans; the three grains together added about 2%. Closed. A free contract archive keeps running and will hold enough curve history to run the real test in two to three years.
lessons: Check that the data exists before writing signal code; the gate took a day and saved the study from a test it couldn't run.
A proxy that only matches plain momentum adds nothing to a book that already runs trend.

extra_tables.title: Share of the proxy's profit by market

vintage: Yahoo futures and fund prices downloaded 2026-10-18, 2011-07-05 to 2026-10-16
